question: Compare how Schwab and Raymond James describe their value proposition to independent advisors.

claims.text: Value proposition - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says Schwab's Advisor Services segment has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs. Management believes it keeps its competitive position mainly through sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams "dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed." It says it pairs superior service with technology that gives RIAs a "highly-developed, scalable platform" for administering client assets.

Value proposition - Schwab: The 2025 10-K describes proprietary advisor software and the Advisor Services website as the core platform for account opening, money movement, transfers, trading and service. It lists integrations with third-party CRM, portfolio-management, trade-order and planning tools. It also lists Schwab Advisor Portfolio Connect (free to advisors), thinkpipes and iRebal.

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building "a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone." He cited more lending support, alternatives capability, an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform with funds from nearly 60 managers, and the launch of Advisor ProDirect for breakaway advisors.

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster called Schwab the "leading custodial offer" and said its "value proposition to advisers has never been stronger." He cited added lending, including a structured asset lending program that lets advisors keep clients' borrowing against alternatives and restricted or private shares in-house. He also said Schwab is enhancing digital RIA workflows (move money, account open, account maintenance) and modernizing advisor-platform tools.

Value proposition - Schwab: The May 2026 investor day deck describes "the leading RIA support ecosystem," providing wealth tools, investment/lending products and technology "in addition to custody & service." It also says Schwab will expand value-added RIA offerings and modernize platforms.

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said the advisor business serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets, on a platform combining custody, trading, banking and lending, technology, and dedicated service and support. He said the business requires scale, trust and operational excellence, and that more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as custodian last year, "more than 3x the number of the next closest provider." The October 2026 press release highlights a partnership with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors to the independent RIAs Schwab serves.

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the FY2025 3Q-era calls (the 2Q25 call was published July 2025 and the 3Q25 call October 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry described a "best of both worlds" value proposition. It combines an "advisor and client-focused culture" with "leading technology and solutions," and he said it resonates across all affiliation options. He added that the firm's strong balance sheet and commitment to independence are a differentiator, and that a stable platform matters amid short-term and leveraged-backed players and industry M&A.

Value proposition - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says the firm's ability to attract advisors rests on its "values-based culture, our commitment to service, and the unique ways in which we provide services to our financial advisors." It cites business coaching and growth tools, and separate national conferences for the employee and independent contractor channels. It describes AdvisorChoice, under which advisors affiliate as employees, as independent contractors, or through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the 1Q FY26 call (published January 2026), Shoukry cited the "largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody," with "critical mass and decades of experience in all of them." He tied this to cultural fit and platform. He also cited the private wealth advisor program, an expanded alternatives platform, and a newly launched proprietary AI operations agent named Rai.

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the call published April 2026, Shoukry said "advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities." He credited a client-focused culture, leading technologies and products, a strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence. He said the firm will keep investing in automation, process improvement and AI as part of a "more than $1.1 billion annual technology spend." On the call published July 2026 he repeated this and cited "near record levels of adviser satisfaction" and investment in private wealth tools.

Value proposition - Raymond James: Its independent-advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-05-19) pitches "A partnership in independence." It says independent contractors can "access our full capabilities at a level that's right for your business" with a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer. It lists private wealth concierge support, advisor-built technology, marketing, business consulting, succession and acquisition guidance, paraplanning, admin extension, and a Corporate RIA model.

Value proposition - Raymond James: The RIA & Custody Services page (page content as of 2026-07-12) says RCS gives RIAs "true strategic, financial and administrative control," "free from retail conflict," using as much or as little of Raymond James's support as needed. It lists a dedicated service associate, transitions management, technology that incorporates third-party applications, marketing, practice management, succession planning and acquisition, and Wealth Strategies for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients.

adjacent.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-28) reports that Wurster told Schwab Impact attendees Schwab will keep focusing on custody for RIAs with under $100 million AUM, saying Schwab's role is "to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive." It was reported in the context of Fidelity's move to push out such firms.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-29) reports Shoukry saying Raymond James has the largest total addressable market because all affiliation options are offered at scale, so advisors can focus on cultural fit and capabilities. The independent contractor channel draws the most dollar interest, and RIA custody is growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

gaps.what: Raymond James Investment Advisors Services, named in the question, does not appear in the evidence. The RIA-custody offer is described only as RIA & Custody Services (RCS), and RJ Financial Services appears only in trade-press mentions, not in the firm's own description of its value proposition.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James 10-K segment description or advisor-recruiting pages for RJ Financial Services and the RIA & Custody Services division
